Trump also launched an attack on the regime’s president, Isaac Herzog, for failing to respond to his request to pardon Netanyahu over corruption charges. In recent months, however, Trump has offered Netanyahu no comparable support. On the contrary, several statements by Trump and members of his team have been interpreted as casting doubt on Netanyahu’s chances of winning the next election.
The deterioration in relations between the two allies is primarily attributed to U.S. involvement in the illegal war against Iran, which American and Israeli circles have blamed on the pressure Netanyahu put on Trump and the plans he presented to him: plans whose failure was subsequently demonstrated by events on the ground.
Netanyahu, a fugitive wanted for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza by the International Criminal Court, does not give up easily. He is prepared to fight for political survival to his last breath and does not hesitate to use every tool and means available to keep himself in power.
For him, the end justifies the means; what he cannot achieve through deception, tactics, and favors, he seeks to accomplish through more of the same.
He knows that the experience of governmental instability exhausted settlers before the current coalition’s victory and the political battle was settled in his favor.
Netanyahu is seeking to heat up various fronts because his supporters on the right and far right are drawn toward escalation and confrontation and are energized by them.
He therefore plans to keep the aggression fronts active, particularly in Gaza, the occupied West Bank, and Lebanon, as well as Syria, given the latitude for aggressive military operations that the U.S. administration has granted it on these fronts.
If the U.S. were to further expand the regime’s room for maneuver toward Iran, which is unlikely at this stage, Netanyahu would not hesitate to resume the aggression against Iran.
That could provide him with the justification he is looking for to postpone the election because of the war, should his fears of defeat grow.
The West Bank, meanwhile, appears to be the electoral arena most suited to the war criminal and the far right, amid the silence of the U.S. administration.
Netanyahu is weighing his options and examining them with considerable calculation in an effort to control the voters’ agenda, so that his government’s failures are pushed to the bottom of the list, particularly the major failure of the October 7 attack.
The shortest, least costly path in security and political terms, and the one most attractive to his right-wing base, appears to be the West Bank. He can deliberately push the situation there toward more deterioration by providing covert and overt support for settler terrorism and their escalating terror attacks against Palestinians and their property.
This would come alongside political measures and continuing international violations, including efforts to take control of UNRWA facilities, most recently the Qalandia Institute, as well as the events in the village of Qusra south of Nablus and the destruction of a Palestinian monument by one of the governing coalition’s lawmakers. It also includes support for and the establishment of additional settlement outposts in Areas A and B.
Netanyahu has already begun circulating media and political leaks suggesting that the Palestinian Authority could collapse, alongside reports that reservists’ leave has been canceled and that combat battalions are being reinforced in the West Bank out of concern over a “security deterioration.”
These leaks are being directed by Netanyahu and his team to shape settler public opinion, mobilizing the right in Netanyahu’s favor, and pushing the October 7 issue down the list of priorities for the public.
In the Gaza Strip, Netanyahu’s rhetoric has grown increasingly threatening as he searches for a pretext to intensify the genocidal war, even if the excuse is children’s kites, to justify escalation and derail the agreement for the second phase of the ceasefire.
Netanyahu understands that he still has time to escape the trap of political collapse by adopting security, political, and media strategies, and that he can benefit from the fragmentation of his opponents.
Ultimately, however, the election will alter little regarding the regime’s status as the primary source of regional insecurity. The reasoning may hinge less on individual personalities and more on a deeply entrenched strategic and political paradigm.
Both Netanyahu and his main challenger Gadi Eisenkot, share hawkish worldviews. Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar (Straight) Party, pioneered the “Dahiyeh doctrine of disproportionate force”. The regime’s political survival is tied to endless war in the region, which has long fuelled its pariah status and international isolation. In essence, the next prime minister, regardless of identity, will retain a confrontational posture, perpetuating the cycle of tension across West Asia.

Asia-Pacific Community: Joint rescue efforts underscore enduring China-Nepal friendship amid deadly mudslide
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
00:03:02 CST
01:03:02 KST

KATHMANDU, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Faced with the catastrophic mudslide disaster battering Nepal's border regions, China has stood firmly with its long-time neighbor with timely assistance and professional rescue support, turning bilateral friendship into tangible life-saving actions and showcasing the spirit of mutual assistance amid adversity.
A fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, buried tunnels, destroyed roads, cut off transportation links, and left over 1,200 dead and more than 4,200 people missing by 6 p.m. local time Wednesday in Nepal.
The unprecedented scale of silt deposition and complex underground environments have posed unprecedented challenges to search and rescue operations, making the disaster far more difficult to tackle than conventional geological catastrophes.
"The situation in the mudslide-hit area has far exceeded expectations -- more severe than any disaster I have seen before," Pan Jiangyuan, who has been engaged in tunnel rescue for over 15 years, told Xinhua. "The tunnel is almost completely blocked by silt -- a situation that is unheard of and extremely rare in tunnel rescue."
Pan is one of the nine Chinese tunnel rescue experts sent to Nepal by the Chinese government, along with four DNA identification experts.
As a team member, Pan worked alongside Nepalese military rescue personnel for several consecutive days, conducting reconnaissance and search missions in designated rescue areas.
"We used a flotation device -- a raft -- with rescuers lying on it and moving forward bit by bit. We also used drones for reconnaissance," he said, explaining that in some areas the silt was so deep that personnel couldn't go in alone on foot.
Reshmi, the press officer at the Nepalese rescue command camp, said that the Chinese rescue team was one of the first international rescue teams that came to Nepal to assist in the search and rescue operations.
"We are working very closely together. This is a joint operation, and we are making joint efforts. We have also exchanged liaison officers to strengthen communication and coordination," he said.
As the relief operation unfolds in phases, China has continued to deliver multi-dimensional, all-round support to Nepal's disaster relief and post-disaster recovery. Since the disaster erupted, China has sent two batches of relief supplies to Nepal, continuously shared real-time meteorological and hydrological data, and provided professional technical consultations and early risk warnings to assist Nepal's risk assessment and emergency response.
Chinese social organizations, enterprises and overseas Chinese communities in Nepal have also actively joined the relief campaign.
The China Foundation for Rural Development has set up a forward operating base along the Trisuli River in Nuwakot, leveraging a local hospital as a comprehensive platform for material storage, personnel scheduling and follow-up medical support.
Zou Zhiqiang, director of the foundation's Nepal office, said that the relief work is being carried out in a scientific, phased manner tailored to evolving disaster needs. The current priority remains life-saving search and rescue. The subsequent stage will focus on recovering the deceased and relevant follow-up arrangements, while the third phase will center on resident resettlement, medical services and livelihood restoration.
"The foundation is preparing materials in advance according to the different needs of each phase. We plan to ship some 22 tonnes of relief supplies from China so that they can be put into use as soon as the follow-up work is fully launched," Zou said.
Huawei, together with local Nepalese operators, immediately launched communication network restoration work to ensure basic communication needs in the affected areas. The Nepal Overseas Chinese Association also initiated a fundraising campaign to aid affected residents.
"In this hour of national grief, PRC's prompt support once again reaffirms the enduring strength of our time-tested bilateral friendship," Nepali President Ram Chandra Poudel wrote on social media.
China's foreign ministry said Wednesday that the country is preparing a third batch of emergency relief supplies to Nepal, including Bailey bridges, epidemic prevention materials and emergency communications equipment, adding that China is ready to send a second group of DNA identification experts based on Nepal's needs.
"This is more than humanitarian assistance. It is a powerful expression of good neighbourliness, solidarity and the longstanding friendship between Nepal and China," Pushpa Raj Pradhan, editor-in-chief of People's Review, said. ■

BRATISLAVA, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- The number of unemployed people in Slovakia increased by 8,300 to 152,800 in the second quarter of this year, the Slovak Statistics Office said on Wednesday, adding that unemployment rate increased by 0.3 percentage point year-on-year to 5.6 percent.

KIGALI, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Leaders, policymakers and development partners on Wednesday called for urgent action, increased investment and stronger public-private partnerships to transform Africa's agri-food systems and address persistent hunger, poverty and unemployment at the Africa Food Systems Forum in Kigali, the Rwandan capital.
Opening the forum, Rwandan Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva said Africa has enormous agricultural potential but must urgently turn its resources into productivity and prosperity.
Nsengiyumva said Africa must move beyond viewing agriculture as a traditional sector and instead position it as a modern and dynamic source of decent employment, entrepreneurship, innovation and economic opportunity, particularly for young people and women.

Vilakati called for greater access to quality seeds, fertilizers, irrigation, mechanization, digital technologies, finance, infrastructure, markets and extension services.
Gerardine Mukeshimana, vice-president of the International Fund for Agricultural Development, similarly stressed the need for stronger investment and private-sector participation to achieve lasting transformation of African food systems.

Former Ethiopian Prime Minister Hailemariam Desalegn warned that Africa's agricultural transformation continues to face deep structural challenges despite two decades of efforts.
He identified productivity, value-chain and implementation-related traps as major barriers to transformation, citing inadequate water control, low-yielding seeds, fragmented markets, post-harvest losses, weak transport and cold-chain infrastructure, trade barriers and limited access to finance.
The forum, which runs from Aug. 31 to Sept. 4, brought together more than 5,000 delegates from over 50 countries, including political leaders, policymakers, researchers, farmers, investors, scientists and development partners. ■

The Lincoln's unusually long deployment was partly driven by the lack of safe access to logistics hubs and ports in the Middle East after attacks from Iran. Over 162 mln children in eastern, southern Africa vulnerable to El Nino: UNICEF
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
00:02:42 CST
01:02:42 KST

NAIROBI, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- More than 162 million children, representing over two-thirds of all children in eastern and southern Africa, live in regions vulnerable to the intensifying 2026/2027 El Nino phenomenon, the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) warned on Tuesday.
According to UNICEF, intensifying droughts, extreme heat and severe flooding threaten children's nutrition, health, education, safety, and access to safe water and sanitation.
Etleva Kadilli, UNICEF regional director for eastern and southern Africa, warned that the threat from El Nino is accelerating and the risks to children are already clear, adding that forecasts provide a narrow yet critical window to act before the worst impacts materialize.
"Across the region, children are facing food and water insecurity, overstretched health services and disrupted learning. Further, major climate shocks will likely push children and the systems they rely on to breaking point," Kadilli said in a statement.
UNICEF assessments highlight compounding and immediate risks for children across Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Madagascar, Malawi, Mozambique, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.
In Somalia, severe flooding could directly affect up to 2.5 million people, fueling displacement and disrupting access to food, healthcare, safe water and education, UNICEF said.
In Ethiopia, tens of thousands of children face heightened risks, particularly in regions already grappling with acute food insecurity and deep vulnerability.
Meanwhile, in South Sudan, a combination of drought, extreme heat and localized flooding threatens to exacerbate food insecurity and malnutrition, trigger disease outbreaks, and compound the risks of famine and large-scale displacement, it said.
Less than 1 percent of international humanitarian assistance is currently allocated to anticipatory action, a critical oversight given its vital role in saving lives, mitigating human suffering and safeguarding hard-won development gains, according to UNICEF.
It said early, flexible financing is essential to blunt the impact of El Nino before conditions deteriorate further.
To address these critical response gaps before impacts peak, UNICEF is calling for urgent investments to scale up nutrition services, including by pre-positioning life-saving supplies and expanding early screening and treatment.
It also called for stronger health systems, improved disease surveillance and vaccination campaigns, safe water access, and measures to keep children learning, including by reinforcing school infrastructure and establishing alternative learning spaces. ■

Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi in Cairo, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. Xi held talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi in Cairo on Wednesday. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu)
CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on China and Egypt to support each other, deepen cooperation, and continue advancing the building of a China-Egypt community with a shared future amid a turbulent international and regional landscape.
Xi made the remarks during his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, while emphasizing China's support for regional countries in building a new security architecture in the Middle East via upholding a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security.
ENHANCING BILATERAL EXCHANGES, COOPERATION
Noting that Egypt was the first Arab and African nation to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China in 1956, Xi said that the older-generation leaders of the two countries led their peoples in striving side by side for national independence and against imperialism and colonialism, forging an unbreakable bond of friendship.
Over the past seven decades, China-Egypt relations have weathered challenges and developed distinctive features of equality and mutual trust, friendship and mutual learning, solidarity and mutual support, as well as win-win cooperation, he said.
Xi said the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has achieved leapfrog development in recent years under the guidance of the two heads of state. The two sides share similar views and have closely aligned strategies in pursuing development and revitalization, improving people's well-being, and upholding international fairness and justice, he added.
Xi emphasized that China and Egypt should firmly support each other, maintain the momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all fields and at all levels, and strengthen exchanges and mutual learning on governance experience.
Xi said the two sides should promote mutually beneficial cooperation, better align their development strategies, tap the potential for cooperation in traditional fields such as infrastructure development, power, agriculture and communications technology, and foster new highlights of cooperation in green energy, electric vehicles, aerospace, the digital economy and modern agricultural technology.
The two sides should promote people-to-people exchanges, comprehensively expand exchanges and cooperation in culture, education, science and technology, health, sports and other fields, and facilitate personnel exchanges and enhance people-to-people bonds, Xi said.
The two sides should strengthen security cooperation, jointly combat transnational crime, deepen international cooperation in anti-corruption, firmly support each other's anti-terror efforts, and safeguard their common security, Xi said.
The two sides should strengthen multilateral collaboration, further enhance coordination and cooperation on multilateral platforms such as the United Nations and the BRICS, jointly promote the development of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, jointly oppose unilateralism and acts of bullying, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system, Xi said.
For his part, Sisi welcomed Xi's historic state visit to Egypt on the occasion of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries.
Sisi said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have developed in a sound and steady manner, and cooperation across various fields has yielded fruitful results.
Egypt firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is committed to further advancing the Egypt-China comprehensive strategic partnership, Sisi added.
Egypt is ready to work with China to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, manufacturing, infrastructure development, finance, science and technology, and new energy, strengthen military and security exchanges, and promote closer people-to-people exchanges, so as to benefit the two peoples and contribute to regional development and prosperity, Sisi said.
Sisi said China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, plays an important and constructive role in international affairs. Egypt is ready to strengthen coordination with China at multilateral platforms, jointly address global challenges, and work together to uphold international fairness and justice, he added.
The two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents on Belt and Road cooperation, artificial intelligence, economic and trade, and industrial and supply chain cooperation.
The two sides also issued a joint statement on further deepening their comprehensive strategic partnership, and signed more than 20 cooperation documents covering such areas as digital economy, science and technology, education, and transportation.
NEW REGIONAL SECURITY ARCHITECTURE
In the talks, Xi raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East, saying that China supports countries in the region in developing good-neighborly and friendly relations.
To promote common security in the region, Xi said that efforts should be made to foster the internal driving force for common security in the region.
People in the Middle East should remain masters of their own affairs, and external interference should be rejected, Xi said, noting that China supports regional countries in strengthening dialogue on peace and security, exploring the building of a new security architecture for the Middle East, and taking their future into their own hands.
Xi said that a comprehensive approach should be adopted to advance common security in the region and that given the multiple hotspots in the Middle East and their close interconnections, comprehensive solutions should be pursued.
The Palestinian issue remains at the core of the Middle East question and should never be overlooked or marginalized, he added.
The foundation for common security should be strengthened through development, Xi said, noting that lasting peace and stability in the Middle East fundamentally depend on development.
China stands ready to work with Middle East countries to safeguard the security of international shipping lanes, advance development cooperation, promote the convergence of interests of regional countries, gradually enhance mutual trust, and eliminate the root causes of the conflict, he said.
Xi urged that international coordination for common security in the region should be strengthened, and the UN Charter and international law should serve as the fundamental principles for handling Middle East affairs.
The international community, especially external powers, should abandon double standards in the Middle East, respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, and safeguard regional peace and stability, Xi added.
He also urged support for the United Nations' effective role in Middle East affairs.
Sisi said that Egypt highly appreciates China's consistent, objective, and impartial stance on the Middle East question, noting that Egypt is committed to promoting de-escalation in the region, resolving conflicts and differences through political means, and advancing regional security and development.
Egypt stands ready to continue strengthening coordination with China to ease tensions in the Middle East, safeguard regional stability, and explore a regional security architecture, Sisi said. ■

Malaria kills 122 in Namibia as cases top 122,000
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-03
00:02:30 CST
01:02:30 KST

WINDHOEK, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Namibia has recorded more than 122,000 confirmed malaria cases and 122 deaths since the beginning of this year, Health and Social Services Minister Esperance Luvindao said Wednesday.
Speaking at the launch of the country's 2026 Indoor Residual Spraying campaign in Divundu in the northeastern Kavango East Region, Luvindao said 122,612 confirmed cases and 9,956 hospital admissions had been recorded nationwide.
She noted that 81 percent of the infections were locally transmitted, while the remaining 19 percent were classified as imported cases.
"Malaria remains stubbornly endemic in 10 out of the 14 regions of our country," Luvindao said, identifying Zambezi, Kavango East, Kavango West, Ohangwena, Omusati, Oshana, Kunene, Oshikoto, Omaheke and Otjozondjupa as affected regions.
The minister said the spraying campaign was launched amid a heightened malaria outbreak that had prompted the government to adjust its prevention and elimination strategy.
A recent external review of Namibia's National Malaria Program Strategy found that the country's malaria diagnosis and case-management protocols remained strong, but efforts to control mosquitoes that transmit the disease had fallen behind, she said.
The review was conducted with the participation of the RBM Partnership to End Malaria, the African Leaders Malaria Alliance and the World Health Organization (WHO).
In response, Namibia will adopt a phased elimination approach based on the intensity of transmission in different areas, according to Luvindao.
The ministry is also finalizing quality-assurance guidelines and strengthening the role of community health workers in malaria testing and treatment.
To reduce imported infections, Namibia plans to formalize cross-border surveillance, data sharing and joint response measures with neighboring Angola, Zambia and Botswana, Luvindao said. The ministry has described it as a key malaria prevention measure but said low household participation has weakened its effectiveness.
Earlier ministry figures cited by the Namibian Broadcasting Corporation showed that only about 40 percent of targeted households were reached during the previous campaign, compared with the WHO-recommended target of 85 percent. ■

Farage suggested he was likely to be interviewed by the standards commissioner soon, as he dismissed the criticism of him for failing to register the £5m gift as a sign of a “complainants’ society”.
The Reform UK leader was pressed during the interview on whether his tone had been out of character this summer, after some inside the party questioned if he had sounded like too much of a victim. Asked about whether he could have taken a sunnier and more optimistic tone instead of an aggrieved one, Farage claimed his family had been targeted with threats to their security and “another huge bout of debanking”.
“Have I been pretty ratty over that and upset over that? I will accept. Hands up. I might not have quite been my normal self over the last few months, but you know when it’s your own family, it’s close to home,” he said. “I’ve been around for ever in this game. I’m big enough and ugly enough to take the rough and tumble in the game. I’ve generally, you know, gone through politics with a smile, whatever’s happened. But some of those personal things over the last few months have weighed very heavily.”
During the interview, Farage appeared to reject any suggestion of a reconciliation with Restore Britain, which is run by the former Reform MP Rupert Lowe and is posing a threat to the party’s vote on the hard right.
The Reform leader accused Lowe of having a “very vindictive motivation” and helping the Conservatives, as well as claiming Restore echoed the language of the 1930s.
“The problem is some people around [Lowe] are saying things that we’ve not heard in this country since the 1930s, if we are being really honest about it ... I think the vote for that is very, very small. I believe, and time will tell, but I believe that the next general election will be a binary choice between the Labour prime minister and Reform. And in that instance, you know, people will use their vote sensibly.”
There had been speculation earlier this summer that Farage could step away from Reform amid scrutiny of his finances and jostling for position among those senior politicians who could succeed him. Reform UK has slipped in some recent polls having led for more than a year, falling behind Labour and even the Conservatives.
Farage told the BBC he would still be leader of the party at the next election. “It’s my responsibility,” he said. “I will be there. To carry the can whichever way it goes.”

Lebanon central bank says new audit to scrutinise transactions for graft
Lebanon's central bank said Wednesday that an outside firm had begun a forensic audit into past transactions linked to its foreign assets, scrutinising them for evidence of graft in the wake of the country's economic collapse.
The move is part of measures the institution has taken to improve oversight, steps that have also resulted in the arrest of the body's former governor, Riad Salameh.
A forensic audit has also been a key demand of the international community and the International Monetary Fund as Lebanon seeks bailout funds after the economic crash, which began in 2019.
The central bank said Wednesday that on August 17 the New York-based Alvarez & Marsal began the forensic audit of "selected transactions", covering the period from October 2019 to the end of 2023.
The audit includes "transactions related to the central bank's foreign assets, including subsidy programmes for essential goods and materials" as well as other transfers, it said.
In May, the central bank had said that the audit aimed to verify that payments and transfers "were executed pursuant to proper authorisations and approvals", and that funds "were used for their intended purposes, without any violation, misuse, or misappropriation".
In 2020, Alvarez & Marsal had launched an audit of the central bank but later halted work after the body failed to hand over necessary data.
The firm resumed that audit the following year, and its preliminary report in 2023 painted a damning picture of the institution under long-serving former governor Salameh.
Salameh, who headed the bank from 1993 to July 2023, is widely viewed as a key culprit in the country's dramatic economic crash and is accused of having amassed a fortune during his time in the job.
He has faced numerous accusations including embezzlement and tax evasion in probes in Lebanon and abroad but has consistently denied any wrongdoing, insisting he is being made a "scapegoat" for the economic collapse.
He was arrested in September 2024 and charged with offences including the alleged embezzlement of $44 million from the central bank, but was released a year later after posting record bail of more than $14 million.
He was placed in custody again in July over accusations including embezzlement and illegal enrichment after a complaint lodged by the new central bank authorities.

Could GLP-1 weight-loss drugs help you live longer?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
15:23:17 UTC
00:23:17 KST

GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are transformational. From helping people lose weight to controlling their blood sugar to tamping down inflammation and improving heart health, these medications herald a new age of medicine. And now a new study in mice suggests that starting semaglutide, a GLP-1 (glucagonlike peptide 1) medication sold under the brand names Wegovy and Ozempic, in old age extends the lifespan by about 12 percent.
Not only that, but semaglutide outperformed dieting in terms of maintaining memory and keeping blood sugar in check. It’s an intriguing result: Scientists already knew that restricting calories seems to boost longevity and hold off the ill effects of aging. But sticking to such a diet is hard, and researchers have long looked for a drug that delivers the same benefits without the hunger. The new results, published in Nature, suggest they may have found it.
In the study, scientists gave semaglutide to female mice that were 20 months old—roughly equivalent in age to a woman in her 60s—and injected them with the drug for the rest of their lives. Against a comparison group of the same age that ate freely and received only saline shots, the mice’s median lifespan rose by about 12 percent—from 742 days to 834.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
Semaglutide’s list of uses has grown long in recent years. Beyond being used to treat diabetes and obesity, it is approved to lower cardiovascular risk, slow kidney decline and treat fatty liver disease, with trial data piling up for sleep apnea and osteoarthritis. Why one drug works in so many seemingly unrelated conditions is a mystery. “I read in journals about all these benefits for all kinds of diseases, and I don’t think there was an answer in the scientific community,” says Danica Chen, a longevity researcher at the University of California, Berkeley, and senior author of the new study.
Chen has researched calorie restriction for two decades and thought that semaglutide might work as a dieting substitute because it also reduces calorie intake, albeit through appetite suppression rather than willpower and discipline. Perhaps, she reasoned, by slowing aging itself through the same calorie restriction effect, the drug would push back the diseases that aging can bring on. It worked.
Mice on semaglutide explored more, balanced longer on a rotating rod, ran farther on a treadmill and solved a maze faster—gains that held even after the researchers accounted for the animals just being leaner than their peers. Compared with the untreated animals, their tissues were less worn out and inflamed, and they died later.
Then Chen and her team set up a separate, five-month experiment in which a group of late-life mice got the drug while another group was simply fed 24 percent less—about the same amount of food as the treated mice had cut back on because of appetite suppression. Semaglutide treatment matched the diet on measures of muscle strength and coordination.
To see whether the drug works through the same biological mechanism as dieting, the team sequenced gene activity in the livers of treated mice and compared that to existing data on calorie restriction. The overlap was significant: both calorie restriction and the GLP-1 quieted down inflammation and fat processing, and both stepped up the genes for handling blood sugar and maintaining proteins. The results suggests semaglutide mimics calorie restriction but has an additional power: the GLP-1 mice had better memory scores, curiosity levels and blood sugar.
“In that sense, it’s more than just a calorie restriction,” Chen says. Why the drug apparently has this edge over dieting is unclear. “The short answer is: we don’t know yet,” she says.
The study doesn’t answer whether dieting or semaglutide extends the lifespan more. “Maybe calorie restriction increases the lifespan more?” wonders Nir Barzilai, a longevity researcher at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine who was not involved in the study. “The data is not there, and it bugs me.” It bugs Chen, too.
That experiment is currently ongoing, she says. “I don’t predict what the results might be. The results always surprise us.”

The risk of high blood pressure in pregnancy is rising—and the damage can be life-changing
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
15:22:57 UTC
00:22:57 KST

It happened so fast.
It was 2019, and Megan O’Grady was 32 weeks pregnant with her first child. She took her dogs for a walk, just as she usually did. But that day, she was surprised by how tired she was. Then her chest started to hurt. Later, sitting in a restaurant with her husband, she felt miserable. She realized something was wrong. By the time she got to the hospital that night, her blood pressure was 220/120 millimeters of mercury (mm Hg)—dangerously high.
O’Grady was shocked: at a doctor visit just a few days before, her blood pressure was completely normal. But now she was suffering from severe preeclampsia—a potentially deadly pregnancy complication marked by high blood pressure and organ damage. She rapidly found herself with no choice but to give birth, more than a month before she was due.
On supporting science journalism
If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
“It was so scary,” she recalls. “He was born, and then they were having to check my blood pressure every hour after he was born. It was crazy.”
O’Grady is far from alone. The rate of high blood pressure in pregnancy has increased by 73 percent between 2016 and 2024, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. This is a rate of about one in 10. What’s more, cases of gestational hypertension—high blood pressure that happens to someone for the first time while they are pregnant—have been rising since 1989, the first year the condition was recorded on birth certificates.
The increase can’t be easily explained by any single cause, says Sarah Kilpatrick, a maternal fetal medicine specialist at Cedars-Sinai in Los Angeles. The average age of people’s first pregnancy is going up, and more people older than age 40 are having babies. More women are having twins and triplets more often because of in vitro fertilization. And women’s body mass indexes (BMIs) have been consistently going up.
Any one of these factors is a risk for high blood pressure, Kilpatrick says, and some people might have more than one. As pregnancies progress, gestational hypertension increases the risk of preeclampsia, which also leads to liver and kidney problems. The condition is diagnosed by blood pressure readings and signs of organ damage in urine or blood tests. It can be fatal: blood pressure problems during pregnancy are one of the leading causes of illness and death in U.S. mothers. And as with O’Grady, the high blood pressure aspect of preeclampsia can come out of the blue.
“If we don’t diagnose it soon enough or people stay pregnant too long, they can get really sick and, in the extreme, of course, die,” Kilpatrick says. “That’s the problem with the disease—it can be very insidious.”
The recent CDC report found that gestational hypertension in 2024 was highest among Native American and Black women. People age 40 and older and those whose BMI was considered “obese” were also most likely to have the condition. But in general, the rates of high blood pressure in pregnancy are rising, no matter what. Baha Sibai, a maternal fetal medicine specialist at in the University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston, believes the rate could be even higher because many birth certificates have incomplete data.
A piece of data that could help doctors better understand and manage hypertension in pregnancy involves tracking how many weeks the pregnancy reached before birth, Sibai says. Once diagnosed, he says, gestational hypertension is supposed to be monitored very carefully in the interest of the woman, not just the fetus.
“All of our focus before was managing the pregnancy,” he says. “Now there is a big emphasis on how we are going to reduce morbidity in the woman.”
Preeclampsia is, at its heart, a systemic response to the placenta. An abnormal increase in a protein called sFlt-1 (soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase 1), which slows down placental growth, Kilpatrick says. This seems to be the trigger that leads to preeclampsia later.
In 2023 the U.S. approved the first blood test to diagnose preeclampsia, measuring the ratio of sFlt-1 to another placental protein that doesn’t change. Kilpatrick was involved getting it approved.
“We’ve known it’s been increasing partially because of better recognition and diagnosis,” Kilpatrick says. Still, some women may not appreciate the risks of hypertension and preeclampsia. “It should be something women know about,” she says.
When O’Grady went to the hospital, she was diagnosed with a severe form of preeclampsia, a rare condition called HELLP syndrome (the acronym is based on symptoms: hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelet levels). The staff immediately gave her magnesium sulfate to prevent her from having seizures.
“I had no concept of what that was,” she says of HELLP syndrome, “no concept that my chest pain was my liver being pushed up” because of swelling and pressure.
High blood pressure in pregnancy carries lifelong consequences, raising the risk of cardiovascular disease and recurring hypertension. This is particularly true for preeclampsia.
O’Grady recovered from her first pregnancy, and she and her husband planned carefully for their second. She went on beta-blockers in case her blood pressure started creeping up again—it did.
At 24 weeks, her blood pressure started to climb, and eventually, she was admitted to a hospital for the remainder of her pregnancy. At 28 weeks, she delivered her baby. The nurses offered to play music in the delivery room. O’Grady chose the Beatles classic “Let It Be.”
“It’s out of your control,” she says, describing that moment years later, with her two sons running around the house. Now she follows a healthy lifestyle that she hopes will ward off the risk of heart disease. “You just have to listen to your doctors and trust in their advice. You kind of have to hope that everything will be okay.”

Hinton’s Views on Consciousness: Explained
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
15:01:50 UTC
00:01:50 KST

This post was originally published on this site.
In recent interviews, Hinton has unabashedly spoken of AI being conscious, among many other claims, such as worrying that AI will fool humans into ceding power to AIs against our best interests, and that AIs ‘really understand’ us.
Here are some short videos of these claims in action.
What strikes me most about these conversations as a philosopher of mind is the complete absence of any explanation as to why Hinton thinks any of this.
Consider, for example, Hinton’s argument for why AI really understands. He states that anybody who regularly uses a chatbot knows that AI understands, using a kind of reductio ad absurdum to make his point. Anyone who denies AI lacks understanding is committed to believing an AI can give you the correct answer to a question without understanding the question. This is absurd, he says, so it’s not true.1
Something must be capable of understanding a question to answer a question. This argument alone might not move you, though the claim itself is not entirely unreasonable. In fact, I’d be willing to accept the claim, though I’d draw a different conclusion to Hinton. I wouldn’t concede AI consciousness on these grounds. Id respond that AI doesn’t actually answer questions. It produces outputs given inputs.
But this is beside the point, because Hinton’s views on AI are rooted in a lot more than the arguments offered in these videos, and that’s what’s frustrating.
What’s absent from the conversation is Hinton’s beliefs on the nature of understanding, how the human brain works, and how these views of his inform his views on AI consciousness and intelligence. That’s what we’ll get into here.
What Does Hinton Think the Brain is Like?
The Symbolic View and The Connectionist View
There are two big views on how the brain works: a symbolic view of the brain (it goes by other names too) and a connectionist view of it.
Hinton is a connectionist. He essentially believes that the human brain is one big neural network, and that, as such, it processes information very similarly to LLMs. Of course, Hinton and everyone else recognises that LLMs learn differently to humans, but he believes that fundamentally the human brain and LLMs are both non-symbolic distributed weight systems (these points are hinted at in the videos above, just not explained in any detail).
According to a connectionist model of the brain, we can explain human cognition in terms of neuronal connections, specifically, in terms of the patterns of activations that emerge across networks of neurons and the strengths of those patterns.
This view of the brain is sharply contrasted with a symbolic view in cognitive science, according to which the brain is like a digital computer. On this view, human cognition is understood in terms of the manipulation of symbols using formal rules.
Consider, then, what it means according to each view, to ‘understand’ something.
The Classic Symbolic View
To understand something according to a classic symbolic view of the brain, one needs to correctly manipulate a specific representation of whatever it is you’re trying to understand (a ‘representation’ of something is basically a fancy word for a physical symbol that carries information about that thing. e.g, that the concept bachelor contains information about males and marriage)
To understand what a bachelor is, you need to possess the appropriate rules to correctly use the term bachelor. Such a rule might be bachelor = unmarried adult male. Possessing an understanding of the concept bachelor on this view, just is the ability to check whether something is a male, is unmarried, and is an adult, and to return an appropriate output, namely, that ‘X is a bachelor’ or that ‘X is not a bachelor’.
The Connectionist View
According to a connectionist view, the brain has no rules and has no physical symbols in this sense. All it has are patterns of activations across neurons and varying strengths among those different patterns. In our last example, the concept bachelor does not consist of any information stored in symbols. And understanding what a bachelor is does not require possessing rules to manipulate that symbol.
It consists of the right neuronal patterns of activations, and those neuronal patterns of activations, further standing in the right relationships to other patterns of neuronal activations that are relevant to the concept.
E.g., to understand what a bachelor is requires the right patterns of neurons to activate to identify a bachelor (e.g., when you encounter one) and to have this neural pattern overlap with other appropriate patterns, for example the activations for ‘unmarried’, ‘male’ and ‘adult’, while diverging from unrelated ones, like ‘women’, ‘child’ and ‘married’.
Why Hinton Thinks AI’s ‘Understand’
For a brief overview of how LLMs work, see section 1 of this article before reading further
Now you’re in a better position to understand why Hinton thinks AIs ‘understand’. He’s a connectionist. He views the brain as one enormously vast and complex neural network, which, though not identical to an LLM, is built of the same basic principles.
LLMs, like the brain, is built on distributed representations and learned weights. So when we ask what it means for an LLM to understand something for Hinton, it more or less means exactly the same thing as what it means for a human to understand something. Once an LLM has been appropriately trained, and its ‘representations’ —that is, its patterns of activations across its MLP and attention layers —stand in the right relationships to the relevant concepts (i.e., other activation patterns) then an LLM understands these concepts. That is why Hinton thinks LLMs understand you when you ask it a question and it gives you the ‘right’ answer.
Now, I want to be clear, connectionism as a theory does not claim to explain consciousness. Moreover, I don’t mean to suggest that all connectionists believe that ‘understanding’ can necessarily be reduced to the picture I have described above (instead, I am interested in offering a possible way of understanding Hinton’s own claims about AI). So, Hinton’s view on consciousness are unexplained based on his connectionism beliefs alone. With that said, I do think we are in a better position to understand his views on consciousness if we consider his connectionist beliefs.
Hinton is well known for having built and designed foundational neural network models. He has even won the Nobel Prize “for foundational discoveries and inventions that enable machine learning with artificial neural networks”2
Now, if you remember that Hinton believes LLMs share the same basic foundational architecture as human brains, it is not too difficult to see how he might believe AIs are conscious. To be honest, if I were convinced the brain was a neural network —and I am really not convinced of this — I would at least consider it incumbent on me to seriously consider whether AI is conscious too.
Now, here comes the kicker. I really don’t see any reason to believe connectionism about the brain is true. But that’ll be a post for another time.
In the meantime, let me say that what is desperately missing in the media is any kind of educational content, or even laying out of background assumptions, to explain the views of people like Hinton. There is no denying Hinton is a man of genius, talent, and exceptional accomplishment. That is all the more reason to make very clear what his background beliefs are. Since, we are already conditioned to believe what he says.
Thank you for being here. If you found this article valuable, consider a free or paid subscription. Behind the paid tier you’ll find work that spells out my own philosophical views, analysis of AI lab papers, videos where I share ideas in progress and more. Plus, you’ll be helping support the existence of rigorous independent philosophical writing on AI consciousness, something we all desperately need today.
See this argument in the first minute of the second video linked here.
See: https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2024/hinton/facts/

China’s Xi visits Egypt’s el-Sisi: Why it matters
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02

China’s Xi visits Egypt’s el-Sisi: Why it matters
Xi’s historic visit to Egypt aims to strengthen China-Egypt ties amid rising Middle East tensions.
Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting Egypt for the first time in a decade, as Cairo looks to foster deeper economic and military ties with Beijing while maintaining its long-standing relationship with Washington.
The visit comes as the US-Israel war on Iran and resulting disruption to global trade have prompted US allies in the region to reassess their strategic relationships. Most recently, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye announced the Mecca Joint Deterrence Agreement, a mutual defence pact.
Recommended Stories
list of 3 items
- list 1 of 3China’s Xi makes first visit to Egypt in a decade, amid regional turmoil
- list 2 of 3China’s Xi makes his first visit to Egypt in a decade
- list 3 of 3Xi, Modi and Putin attend SCO summit: What’s on the agenda?
Seeking closer ties with Beijing, therefore, is part of an effort to further what President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi has called Cairo’s “independent foreign policy”.
For China, Egypt offers an important foothold in the Middle East with its large economy, control of the Suez Canal and diplomatic influence across the Arab world and Africa.
Here is what you need to know:
What is the visit about?
Xi’s three-day visit, which began on Tuesday evening, includes talks with el-Sisi that are expected to focus on the regional conflict and its consequences for maritime trade security, as well as expanding Chinese investment in Egypt.
The two countries are expected to sign economic agreements covering areas including artificial intelligence (AI), transport and manufacturing.
The visit marks 70 years of diplomatic relations between Egypt and China. Egyptian state-run media reported that Xi has called for the two countries to “expand the scope of pragmatic collaboration”, while el-Sisi praised Chinese investment in Egypt and reiterated Cairo’s support for Beijing’s position on Taiwan, the island nation that China claims as part of its own territory.
Military cooperation is another increasingly important part of the relationship.
In August, Egypt and China held joint air exercises including Chinese J-16 fighter jets and Egypt’s French-made Rafale aircraft. It was the first time the J-16s had taken part in a combat exercise alongside the Rafales.
Why is this state visit important?
Xi’s visit highlights Beijing’s efforts to expand its influence in a region where the US has been the dominant military power for decades.
Egypt is a key Middle East ally for Washington, and the second-largest recipient of US military aid.
The meeting comes at a time of considerable geopolitical instability, with Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, the US-Israel war with Iran, and disruption around the Red Sea caused by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis targeting Saudi-linked ships all raising questions about the durability of the existing US-led regional order, experts say.
Rob Geist Pinfold, a lecturer in international security at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera, “China is trying to position itself as an increasingly important economic and diplomatic actor in that environment, particularly as a counterweight to the US, as a more responsible and more hands-off regional actor.”
Egypt has a population of 110 million and is an important market for Chinese goods and investment. It is also particularly important to Beijing because it controls the Suez Canal, Pinfold said, adding that the waterway has become even more critical amid disruptions to shipping in the crucial Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz straits.
Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz for the past six months in retaliation for US-Israeli strikes. Prior to the war, more than one-fifth of the world’s oil and petroleum products were shipped through the strait, which is the only sea route to the open ocean available to Gulf producers.
China offers Egypt opportunities to develop investment, infrastructure and technology, while bilateral ties have also expanded into areas including defence and artificial intelligence.
But the growing relationship should not be interpreted as Egypt pivoting away from the US entirely, Pinfold said, noting that “instead, el-Sisi’s approach is better understood as one of diversification and strategic autonomy”.
“In short,” Pinfold said, “as the Gulf states have done in recent years, he is trying to hedge without alienating or annoying Egypt’s indisputably most important ally, the US.”
How strong are Egypt-China relations?
Relations between Cairo and Beijing have deepened significantly since 2014, when el-Sisi visited China and the two countries signed a strategic partnership agreement.
China is now Egypt’s largest trading partner in non-petroleum goods, with bilateral trade reaching nearly $20.7bn by the end of 2025, according to Egypt’s State Information Service (SIS).
Data from the country’s Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS) shows a nearly 200 percent increase in Egyptian exports to China, at $840.8m in the first half of 2026, while imports stood at $10.4bn.
Beijing has also invested more than $10bn in Egypt, including in the New Administrative Capital east of Cairo and an electric rail line serving industry in the Nile Delta.
Chinese companies have also invested in container ports, green hydrogen, iron pipes, tyres and satellites.
Chinese investments in Egypt are focused mainly in the Suez Canal area and the China-Egypt TEDA cooperation zone in Ain Sokhna, part of Beijing’s Belt and Road Initiative, which hosts about 200 companies with investments exceeding $3.8bn, according to Egyptian state media.
In 2023, Egypt joined BRICS, the bloc of Global South nations including Brazil, Russia, India and China.

Best Pizza Cheese for Melting and Stretchiness

Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02

00:00:29 KST

Best Pizza Cheese for Melting and Stretchiness
When it comes to pizza, cheese is not just a topping; it is the foundation of texture, flavor, and visual appeal. The perfect pizza cheese should melt smoothly, stretch generously when sliced, and complement the crust and sauce. Achieving that iconic cheese pull depends on protein structure, moisture content, fat levels, and how the cheese is processed. Below is a detailed guide to the best cheeses for melting and stretchiness, along with why they work so well on pizza.
Mozzarella, The Gold Standard!
Mozzarella is widely considered the best pizza cheese for both melting and stretchiness, and for good reason. But why is it that good? Because it has high moisture and an elastic protein structure allow it to melt evenly, and Casein proteins form long strands when heated, creating the classic cheese pull. Also, Mild flavor lets the sauce and dough shine. Calindairy Mozzarella cheese is the best for American or Italian-style pizza.
Types of mozzarella
- Low-moisture mozzarella (whole milk): The most common choice for professional pizzerias. It melts smoothly, stretches well, and releases less water than fresh mozzarella.
- Low-moisture mozzarella (part-skim): Slightly less creamy but still very stretchy. Often used for cost efficiency.
- Fresh mozzarella: Soft and delicate with excellent melt, but high moisture can make pizza watery unless properly drained and baked at high temperatures.
Provolone, Stretch with Extra Flavor!
Provolone is a semi-hard Italian cheese that melts beautifully and stretches well, though slightly less than mozzarella. This cheese had a similar protein structure to mozzarella. Higher fat content adds richness, and more pronounced flavor enhances depth.
Best use of Provolone Cheese
- Blended with mozzarella for better flavor complexity.
- Excellent on Sicilian, Detroit-style, or pan pizzas.
Fior di Latte, Artisan-Level Stretch!
Fior di latte is a fresh mozzarella made from cow’s milk, commonly used in traditional Italian pizzas. Has exceptionally smooth melt, Clean, milky stretch with a soft bite, and Balanced moisture when baked properly.
Best use
- High-temperature ovens.
- Thin-crust pizzas where ingredient quality is the focus.
Oaxaca Cheese, Outstanding Stretch Alternative!
Oaxaca cheese, traditionally used in Mexican cuisine, is one of the stretchiest cheeses available, so you can use it in your next pizza recipe and enjoy the ultimate and extraordinary cheese pull. The pasta filata (stretched curd) process is similar to that of mozzarella. This cheese creates dramatic, long cheese pulls and has a mild flavor that works well with tomato-based sauces.
Normally Can be used for:
- Fusion-style pizzas.
- Home cooks seeking maximum stretch with minimal effort.
Monterey Jack, Smooth Melter with Elasticity!
Monterey Jack melts easily and smoothly, producing moderate stretch. The combination of Monterey Jack and mozzarella cheese is perfect for your signature in cooking a perfect pizza. If you want to have a perfect pizza that could never be found in another place, you should definitely try that combo! Monterey Jack has high moisture content, a soft texture that allows for even melting, and a creamy mouthfeel.
What is the usage of Monterey Jack?
- Blended with mozzarella for added creaminess.
- White pizzas or mild-flavored toppings.
Cheese Blends, Optimizing Melt and Stretch!
Many pizzerias use blends to balance stretch, melt, browning, and flavor.
Popular combinations:
- Mozzarella + Provolone: Improved stretch with deeper flavor.
- Mozzarella + Monterey Jack: Creamier melt with good elasticity.
- Mozzarella + Low amounts of Cheddar: Better browning and flavor, but limited stretch if overused.
Different fat and moisture levels create a more controlled melt and Enhanced flavor without sacrificing texture.
Cheeses to Use Sparingly or Avoid for Stretch!
Some cheeses melt well but do not stretch, while others resist melting altogether.
- Cheddar: Breaks into oil and solids when overheated. You can order cheese pizza and blend it with natural cheese to create a unique taste, and also avoid too much stretch.
- Parmesan: Adds flavor but no stretch.
- Feta and goat cheese: Softens but does not melt smoothly.
These are best used as secondary toppings rather than the main cheese.
Key Factors That Affect Cheese Stretch
If you want to have an ultimate cheese pull, remember the following information:
- Moisture: Moderate moisture allows proteins to loosen without releasing excess water.
- Fat content: Fat enhances meltability, but too much can reduce elasticity.
- Shredding method: Hand-shredded cheese melts better than pre-shredded cheese, which often contains anti-caking agents.
- Baking temperature: Higher heat promotes better stretch and faster melting.
For the best balance of melting and stretchiness, low-moisture whole milk mozzarella remains the top choice. For enhanced flavor and texture, blending it with provolone or Monterey Jack is ideal. If maximum stretch is the priority, Oaxaca cheese is a surprisingly excellent alternative. Choosing the right cheese and using it correctly can elevate pizza from good to unforgettable.

I was once ashamed to admit I’d been strangled nonconsensually during sex. Now I’m speaking up to save women’s lives | Hannah Ferguson
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
15:00:28 UTC
00:00:28 KST

Last week, a 16-year-old girl was found unresponsive in a home on Sydney’s northern beaches. She was airlifted to hospital and died two days later. New South Wales police are investigating her death as the result of a sexual strangulation act. Sources told the ABC the deceased may have experienced a seizure following asphyxiation, and that officers were told the sex was consensual.
While that investigation has yet to run its course, speaking generally, strangulation during sex is not a new phenomenon or conversation. Just a few years ago it was relatively taboo to criticise this normalisation of violence in sex – it was often framed as “anti-kink” to raise concern about this dangerous act that is increasingly depicted in mainstream pornography.
In 2024, Australian research affirmed the prevalence of sexual strangulation. The Archives of Sexual Behaviour published data revealing that 57% of Australians aged 18 to 35 had been strangled at least once during sex, and 51% said they had strangled a sexual partner.
Not only are reports of this act increasing, so are the reports of health impacts. Denele Crozier, the CEO of Women’s Health NSW, stated that since 2023 there had been a 123% increase in women presenting with concerns of a possible brain injury linked to strangulation.
I was previously ashamed to share my own experiences of being strangled during sex nonconsensually. Despite being an outspoken, progressive woman, I froze up and dissociated. Afterwards, I remember questioning whether my response was one of being in shock and afraid for my safety, or if I felt “prudish” if I spoke up and as if I’d be ruining the mood. For a long time, I was embarrassed to admit that while I intellectually knew something wasn’t right, I still failed to call it out in a moment of uncertainty.
That is exactly the concern I have for so many women who may be experiencing sexual strangulation. Affirmative consent is incredibly hard to achieve in these contexts; sexual strangulation is now commonplace and we are not equipped with the sophisticated sex education to match.
In 2022, consent advocate Chanel Contos wrote about this: “Another US study found that 58% of female college students have been choked during sex, further suggesting that this ‘kink’ is becoming increasingly common in younger age demographics. This study found that while many women enjoyed choking, others did it largely to please their sexual partner. This is the real kicker. The problem here is not only that women are being choked during sex without giving consent, but that a lot of the time they are ‘consenting’ not because they derive their own sexual pleasure from it, but because they think it turns the guy on.”
Violence against women and girls has been normalised to such an extent that pornography is convincing us it is normal to be strangled during intimacy, and that we are supposed to like it. I appreciate that messages from leaders like “talk to your kids” are made in good faith, but conversation cannot combat the nature and influence of sex content depicting violence as a standard part of sexual intercourse. We are teaching young men that perpetrating violent acts that have the potential to kill are erotic, and we are teaching women to endure having their lives threatened under the guise of pleasure.
There are people who engage with control of breath as part of particular kinks, but even in acknowledging these consensual engagements, it is important to reiterate that there is no safe way to engage in strangulation.
In response to this expanding dialogue, the social services minister, Tanya Plibersek, has shown her support for Australia to adopt legislation that was introduced to the UK in 2025, making it a criminal offence to possess or publish pornography depicting suffocation or strangulation. I want to add my voice to the many calling for the Albanese government to legislate this imminently.
The government is also, rightly, considering a second significant piece of reform proposed by Contos and her organisation Teach Us Consent. Contos has been campaigning for the government’s digital duty of care legislative drafting to adopt their “Fix Our Feeds” pitch, regulating big tech companies to ensure algorithms are an opt-in feature. This would introduce a consent-based model that allows users to have more control over the information these platforms are serving us, reducing the extremist material that so many are exposed to.
Our government has established that they are willing to take on the regulation of big tech. Australia was the first country in the world to legislate a social media ban for under-16s. We know we have the capability; now it’s time to introduce something that would actually be effective – and give power back to individual users.
These would be two significant steps from the government, after last week’s national cabinet meeting where the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, discussed violence against women and children with state and territory leaders. The subsequent announcements of frameworks and reviews were weak. We need politicians to meet the moment. The safety of women and girls depends on tangible action, now.

====================================================================================================

Latin America’s China Dilemma: Lessons From Peru and Colombia’s Presidential Elections
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
14:18:00 UTC
23:18:00 KST

The recent results of Latin America’s electoral super-cycle (2025–2026) suggest that China has become an increasingly important feature of regional politics. While Beijing’s overall popularity in the region is at an all-time high, Latin Americans are voting in candidates who position themselves as U.S.-aligned and, at times, China skeptics.
The ideological pendulum seems to be swinging to the right, and with it, the region’s place in the broader China-U.S. geostrategic competition is shifting. Even Peru and Colombia, where China policy did not initially appear likely to become a decisive electoral fault line, have elected candidates who are expected to distance their governments from Beijing, at least rhetorically, and move closer to Washington. But in both countries, deep economic ties with China will continue to constrain any significant strategic realignment.
Once in office, then, many of these governments fail to live up to Washington’s expectations. Rather than distancing themselves from Beijing or limiting Chinese investment, they more often adopt a more pragmatic approach in their relations with China while shifting their diplomatic rhetoric closer to the United States.
Honduran President Nasry Asfura campaigned on re-establishing diplomatic relations with Taiwan and severing ties with Beijing. Nearly a year into his presidency, however, no such shift has occurred.
Chilean President José Antonio Kast, who was seen at the U.S.-backed Shield of the Americas Summit while still president-elect, did cancel a controversial Chinese submarine cable project. Still, the broader relationship with China has remained rather stable, with Foreign Minister Francisco Pérez Mackenna making a visit to China in August.
Even the sale of Chilean copper – a critical mineral of strategic concern for Washington – to Chinese importers is at its highest level in nine months.
How will these trends play out in Peru and Colombia, which installed new presidents in July and August, respectively?
Peru
In Peru, the election of right-wing politician Keiko Fujimori to the office of president appears on the surface to be the ideal outcome for Washington. Over the last decade, Peru has been plagued by political instability, with China playing a role in the most recent constitutional crisis. These dynamics suggest that the new administration in Lima would favor closer ties with the U.S. and distance itself from China.
Although Washington will certainly have leverage with the new administration, it remains uncertain whether Fujimori will take a hard line against Beijing. There are two factors that make this unlikely: Fujimori’s political background and Peru’s deep economic ties with China.
Keiko Fujimori is the daughter of the late Alberto Fujimori, a former Peruvian president turned authoritarian ruler, whose constitutional reforms and self-coup are considered by many as the source of the continued political instability that Peru has suffered for most of the 21st century. Alberto Fujimori fundamentally reoriented Peru toward Asian markets during the 1990s, laying the foundations for today’s economic relationship with China.
Keiko Fujimori was elected on a platform built under her father’s controversial and authoritarian legacy, one that coupled gross human rights violations with economic growth. Some experts suggest that she will continue her father’s legacy on the China question by adopting a pragmatic approach of political alignment with Washington and economic engagement with Beijing.
After all, China remains Peru’s largest trading partner and a major investor across strategic sectors, including mining, energy and infrastructure. For its part, Beijing sees in Lima a strategic anchor, particularly considering Chinese state-owned shipping company COSCO’s investment in the Chancay Port.
The reversal of a Peruvian court ruling that initially curbed state oversight over Chancay port showcases that Lima’s China policy is at a crossroads. Whether Peru would follow Panama’s path and take back the Chancay port or adopt a more equidistant approach to both superpowers will depend on decisions made by Fujimori – and, most importantly, on Peru’s Constitutional Tribunal upcoming ruling on oversight rights over the port.
Colombia
In Colombia, Abelardo de la Espriella’s presidential victory brought another rightward shift in the region’s electoral politics. De la Espriella has pledged to prioritize relations with democratic states within the Western hemisphere, vowing to sever diplomatic ties with both Nicaragua and Cuba and saying that his administration will have “no ties whatsoever with tyrannies.” It remains to be seen whether the same ideological approach will shape relations with a non-democratic superpower like China.
De la Espriella has also promised to normalize relations with the United States following the cooling of bilateral ties and rifts between President Gustavo Petro and U.S. President Donald Trump. The U.S. remains Colombia’s top trading partner with longstanding commercial, political and military ties in Bogotá.
And yet, de la Espriella’s foreign policy doctrine does not seem to be distancing from Beijing as expected. One of his stated priorities is to commercialize Colombia’s foreign policy by turning ambassadors and diplomats into “gestores comerciales,” or facilitators of trade.
The balance de la Espriella’s government is trying to strike was recently put to a test on X. China’s ambassador to Bogotá, mirroring the now largely defunct “wolf warrior diplomacy,” publicly questioned the Colombian vice president’s motives after China was not invited to a meeting with a group of states that gave humanitarian assistance to the South American nation after an earthquake. Although the vice president quickly de-escalated the exchange and asked the ambassador to convey his concerns through adequate diplomatic channels, this incident illustrates how difficult it is to balance out an actor that perceives itself as being cornered throughout the region by its peer competitor.
It appears that under de la Espriella, Colombia’s economic relations may become increasingly compartmentalized from broader geopolitical disagreements. If that is the case, Beijing can adjust by narrowing its engagement with Bogotá to trade and investment, preserving the economic relationship, and avoiding more sensitive ideological disputes.
What’s Next?
Peru and Colombia have set the table for Latin America’s biggest election of the year: the October general election in Brazil. The results could prove to be consequential for China’s standing in Latin America. As it stands, Beijing has signaled support for continuity with current President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is running for re-election. His main rival, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son and political heir of former President Jair Bolsonaro, has positioned himself closer to Trump-aligned forces and a more explicitly pro-U.S. foreign policy.
Senator Bolsonaro has sharply increased his criticism of Brazil’s relationship with China during Lula’s term, even accusing the current president of “bootlicking China” and subverting national sovereignty. He believes that Brazil has become dependent on China, with Brasilia acting as a mere exporter of raw materials while receiving high-tech goods.
His broader plan consists of leveraging Brazil’s critical minerals and rare earth reserves to partner with the U.S. and to reduce U.S. dependencies on Chinese supply chains. Bolsonaro’s criticism of China, combined with Argentine President Javier Milei’s recent trip to Brazil to campaign on his behalf, sharpened Beijing’s concern about the country’s electoral outcomes.
In that context, Chinese President Xi Jinping expressed support for Lula in “opposing external interference,” while the two leaders also agreed on the need to speed up negotiations on a Mercosur-China agreement.
Conclusion
China policy featured in the electoral politics of Peru and Colombia, and the Brazilian presidential elections are next. The results of Latin America’s 2025-2026 electoral super cycle, together with developments in Cuba and Nicaragua, where U.S. pressure is set to increase in the upcoming months, suggest that China’s space for political maneuver is shrinking.
But this doesn’t mean that the region is on the verge of a clean realignment. As shown by developments in Honduras, Chile, and Argentina, political alignments are one thing, and commercial ties are another. The latter, at times, can obscure the former.
Beijing can no longer assume that deep economic ties will shield it from electoral backlash, sovereignty concerns, or pressure from Washington. At the same time, its role in trade, infrastructure, mining, and investment gives it a resilience that campaign rhetoric alone cannot easily undo.
If Peru, Colombia, and Brazil teach us anything, it is that the future of China’s role in Latin America will be shaped less by campaign promises than by the region’s ability to create alternatives. Without those alternatives, even the most China-skeptical governments will remain constrained by the economic map they inherit.

UNEP urges sustained action to cap global warming, avert climate breakdown
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-02
22:17:26 CST
23:17:26 KST

NAIROBI, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Governments, industries, and societies must take radical measures to prevent global temperatures from breaching the 1.5-degree-Celsius warming limit set by the Paris Agreement and avert widespread calamities such as extreme heatwaves and ecosystem collapse, according to a United Nations Environment Program (UNEP) report launched in Nairobi on Wednesday.
The report "Limiting Overshoot: Navigating exceedance of 1.5 degrees Celsius and pathways towards return" warns that failing to curb runaway warming will plunge humanity into a perilous future marked by climatic shocks, hunger, disease outbreaks, and economic collapse.
UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen noted that while global temperatures are increasingly likely to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels in the near term, avoiding a permanent breach of the threshold remains entirely possible.
"Now is the time we must double down on climate action. We can -- and must -- get on the right path by cutting greenhouse gas emissions, strengthening resilience and adaptation, and ensuring that any exceedance of 1.5 degrees Celsius is as small and short-lived as possible," Andersen said.
She noted that preventing even a fraction of a degree of warming each year will save lives, protect fragile ecosystems, and reduce economic losses.
Despite national net-zero commitments, the UNEP report warns that breaching the Paris Agreement's temperature threshold is increasingly likely, escalating risks of accelerated sea-level rise, coral reef collapse, catastrophic wildfires, and glacier loss.
The report warns of an elevated risk of triggering irreversible tipping points such as the collapse of the West Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets, the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, and the Amazon rainforest, with catastrophic consequences for planetary stability.
Unabated emissions of greenhouse gases, including methane and carbon dioxide, could cause temperatures to continue rising, threatening small island developing states and low-lying coastal cities with partial or total submersion, the report notes.
The report says that runaway warming will drive up energy costs and insurance premiums, straining financial systems worldwide.
Stressing that a climate crisis is still preventable, the report emphasizes that nations must transition to clean energy while cutting emissions of methane and other short-lived climate pollutants.
Limiting temperature spikes will require simultaneous adaptation and mitigation efforts, backed by multilateral cooperation, political resolve, effective policies, and sustained financing, according to the report.
The report calls for implementing simultaneous adaptation and mitigation measures, backed by multilateral action, political goodwill, effective policies, and sustained financing, to curb global temperature spikes. ■
